cells.tense: You are the one aiming this, and the aim is holding steady right now.
cells.ask: Tell one person which way you're pointed today. Not the plan, just the heading. Let the saying be the whole act.
cells.core:
You know which way this goes, and it isn't loud. You pick the direction, you mean it, and the call doesn't need defending — it carries itself once it's pointed. Other people feel it as steadiness rather than force.
The quiet part is real too. Something in you holds a read on a situation before it says anything, and that holding is doing work. It's why the decisions land. What this balance costs to keep is that you keep trusting the read before it's confirmed — no committee, no second opinion, just the call and the moving. That cost only gets paid if the direction is yours, so it's worth knowing where you picked it up.
cells.sheetLine: You choose the direction and you mean it, quietly.
cells.verb: Moving with the direction already decided, no announcement needed
cells.place: At the point where the course gets chosen

cells.tense: You are already living in how this will land, and none of it has happened yet.
cells.ask: Pick one decision you've already made and tell someone why, without arguing the case. If the case needs arguing, it wasn't decided.
cells.core:
You're steering toward an outcome that's still forming, and your grip has gotten ahead of it. Decisions come fast because you can see the whole structure in advance — so you're bracing for a version of events that hasn't arrived, and treating it as the thing to manage now.
The cost shows up in the room you're actually in. People get the conclusion before the situation has had its say, and the certainty that usually serves you starts to feel like pressure. The structure is real; the timing is what's off. When this is working, things make sense in your presence — clear, solid, no arm-wrestling. Here you're borrowing tomorrow's authority to settle today, and that costs you the read that would have made it unnecessary.
cells.sheetLine: You're settling tomorrow before today has spoken.

cells.tense: You stopped choosing, and you're still standing at the last place you chose.
cells.ask: Finish one small piece this week that you've already decided — an outline, a list, a first cut. Do the making and let it stand.
cells.core:
There's a direction you set down and haven't picked back up. Not because you don't know it — you do — but because there's a spot you haven't stepped past, and standing at it has taken the place of moving. The aim is there. The pointing stopped.
The other side of this is plain: a clear call, made once, that others can lean on without asking. That comes back through something small and real to hold onto — making a thing where the structure is obvious and the stakes are low. Small and finished beats large and stalled. Let the making pull you forward, and the picking-back-up will follow it.
cells.sheetLine: You know the direction but you stopped pointing at it.

cells.tense: You are already steering this whole thing and you talk about it like it happened on its own.
cells.ask: Say the word 'I' about one decision you've been describing as the situation requiring it. One sentence, to yourself or someone else.
cells.core:
You're setting the direction here — the calls, the priorities, the pace — and your account of it leaves you out. The steering is yours, and the story treats it as a fact of the landscape. That's not modesty and it isn't confusion. It's your hand on the wheel with nobody's name on it.
Something simpler is available. This whole line started as one plain act: this, not that, and meaning it. Not the whole architecture — just the first motion, chosen and owned. When this is working, people trust the structure because it visibly serves what it organizes, and you're visible inside it. That's what's been missing, and it's smaller than it looks. Worth saying, once, without the smoothing.
